title: Symbolism & the Pre-Raphaelites
description: Dreamlike myth, doomed romance, and veiled mystery from the later 19th century.

items.title: Ophelia
items.description_narrative: John Everett Millais's *Ophelia* vividly captures the tragic moment of Ophelia's drowning, as described in Shakespeare's *Hamlet*. The artwork is renowned for its meticulous detail in depicting the surrounding flora and Ophelia's ethereal pose, painted from a model floating in water.
items.tags: ophelia, shakespeare, pre-raphaelite, victorian art, tragedy, nature, detail, melancholy

items.title: Christ in the House of His Parents
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts the young Jesus in Joseph's carpentry workshop, where a symbolic wound on his hand is tended by Mary, observed by Joseph and Saint Anne. The scene is rich with Christian symbolism and meticulous naturalistic detail, a hallmark of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, christian, religious, symbolism, family, realism, victorian, narrative

items.title: Proserpine
items.description_narrative: Dante Gabriel Rossetti's 'Proserpine' depicts the mythological queen of the Underworld, identifiable by the half-eaten pomegranate she holds. Her mournful expression conveys a sense of exile and entrapment in the shadowy realm.
items.tags: mythology, portraiture, pre-raphaelite, symbolism, classical, melancholy, female figure, aestheticism

items.title: Beata Beatrix
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts Dante Alighieri's Beatrice Portinari at the moment of her death, a subject deeply personal to Rossetti after the death of his wife. It features symbolic elements like a dove delivering a poppy, representing both a spiritual transition and an opiate-induced slumber.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, symbolism, allegorical, portrait, death, love, spiritual, melancholic

items.title: The Day Dream
items.description_narrative: The Day Dream portrays Jane Morris, a prominent muse, in a pensive moment amidst a verdant landscape, embodying Rossetti's ideal of beauty. She holds a honeysuckle branch, symbolizing love, and her distant gaze evokes a profound state of introspection and reverie.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, victorian, portrait, symbolism, female figure, contemplation, romance, jane morris

items.title: Lady Lilith
items.description_narrative: Dante Gabriel Rossetti's 'Lady Lilith' depicts the mythical first wife of Adam, captured in a moment of languid introspection as she admires her reflection. This iconic Pre-Raphaelite work explores themes of female beauty, vanity, and the alluring, often dangerous, power attributed to the archetypal femme fatale.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, symbolism, female figure, mythology, sensuality, portrait, beauty, victorian era

items.title: The Awakening Conscience
items.description_narrative: This painting captures a woman's moment of sudden spiritual awakening, her gaze fixed outwards as she rises from a man's lap. Hunt meticulously renders details within the lavish, confined interior, symbolizing the woman's moral predicament and nascent realization.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, victorian, moral allegory, oil painting, awakening, conscience, symbolic, narrative

items.title: The Golden Stairs
items.description_narrative: Edward Burne-Jones's masterpiece depicts a graceful procession of young women descending a spiral staircase, rendered in delicate hues of white and cream. The artwork is celebrated for its ethereal beauty and the serene harmony of its figures.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, victorian art, aestheticism, women, procession, allegory, english painting, dreamlike

items.title: The Beguiling of Merlin
items.description_narrative: This painting by Edward Burne-Jones illustrates the Arthurian legend of Nimue enchanting the wizard Merlin. Nimue, reading from a spellbook, entraps a helpless Merlin within a hawthorn bush, characteristic of the artist's detailed and mythical style.
items.tags: arthurian legend, mythology, pre-raphaelite, symbolism, enchantment, sorcery, victorian art

items.title: King Cophetua and the Beggar Maid
items.description_narrative: Edward Burne-Jones's masterpiece depicts the legendary King Cophetua, who, having scorned all women, falls in love with the humble beggar maid Penelophon as she sits on his throne. The painting captures a moment of quiet reverence, highlighting the king's profound admiration and the maiden's poised humility within an idealized setting.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, symbolism, victorian art, legendary narrative, idealized beauty, romance, melancholic

items.title: The Lady of Shalott
items.description_narrative: John William Waterhouse's iconic painting depicts the tragic Lady of Shalott from Tennyson's poem, captured at the moment she leaves her island tower to face her doom. Her gaze fixed towards Camelot, she sits in a boat amidst unraveling tapestry threads, embodying a pivotal moment of fate and consequence.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, victorian, painting, literature, arthurian legend, symbolism, tragic, romanticism

items.title: Hylas and the Nymphs
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts the mythological youth Hylas being enticed by water nymphs, who emerge from a tranquil pool. Their captivating gazes and outstretched arms draw Hylas towards his tragic fate, as he was eventually drowned by them.
items.tags: greek mythology, nymphs, hylas, pre-raphaelite, oil painting, classical, alluring, tragic

items.title: Ophelia
items.description_narrative: John William Waterhouse's 'Ophelia' vividly portrays the tragic character from Shakespeare's Hamlet, shown moments before her death by drowning. She lies amidst the water's edge, surrounded by lush flora, her gaze distant and resigned.
items.tags: ophelia, shakespearean, literary, pre-raphaelite, victorian, figurative, melancholy, tragic

items.title: The Magic Circle
items.description_narrative: A solitary sorceress, clad in flowing robes, intently draws a fiery magic circle on the earth with a wand, preparing for a mystical ritual. Her enigmatic gaze and the presence of a crow and toad lend an air of ancient power and arcane mystery to the scene.
items.tags: magic, witch, ritual, symbolism, pre-raphaelite, victorian art, fantasy, mysterious

items.title: Work
items.description_narrative: Ford Madox Brown's seminal painting "Work" meticulously depicts a complex street scene in London, centering on the physical labor of navvies engaged in road construction. Surrounding these manual laborers are numerous figures representing different social strata, offering a detailed social commentary on Victorian society.
items.tags: victorian, social realism, pre-raphaelite, labor, urban scene, detailed, symbolic

items.title: The Last of England
items.description_narrative: This iconic painting captures a poignant moment of departure, showing a couple gazing out from a ship as they leave England forever. It powerfully conveys the emotional hardship and social realities of emigration during the mid-19th century.
items.tags: emigration, pre-raphaelite, 19th century, england, farewell, departure, social commentary

items.title: The Apparition
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's 'The Apparition' depicts Salome in a decadent palace, captivated by the ethereal vision of John the Baptist's severed head floating before her. This richly detailed and symbolic work embodies the heightened fantasy and mystical themes characteristic of Symbolism.
items.tags: salome, biblical, symbolism, mystical, macabre, ornate, vision

items.title: Jupiter and Semele
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's 'Jupiter and Semele' depicts the tragic climax of the myth where Jupiter, revealing his true divine form, causes the mortal Semele to perish from his overwhelming glory. The painting is renowned for its intricate detail, jewel-like colors, and the deeply mystical atmosphere characteristic of the Symbolist movement.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, classical, tragedy, mystical, ornate, french art

items.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's "Oedipus and the Sphinx" captures the intense mythological encounter between Oedipus and the Sphinx, who poses her deadly riddle before him. The painting's intricate details and brooding atmosphere exemplify Moreau's Symbolist approach to classical themes.
items.tags: symbolism, mythology, classical, oedipus, sphinx, french art, academic art, fantastic

items.title: The Cyclops
items.description_narrative: Odilon Redon's 'The Cyclops' depicts the one-eyed giant Polyphemus gazing tenderly at the sleeping nymph Galatea, who remains oblivious. This captivating work merges classical mythology with the artist's unique visionary style, inviting contemplation of hidden desires and the power of the subconscious.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, cyclops, galatea, fantastic, dreamlike, french art, classical myth

items.title: Isle of the Dead
items.description_narrative: Arnold Böcklin's "Isle of the Dead" depicts a lone figure in a rowboat approaching a rugged island dominated by cypress trees and monumental rock formations. This iconic work evokes a somber, mysterious atmosphere, often interpreted as a symbolic journey towards the afterlife.
items.tags: symbolism, landscape, death, melancholic, mystery, fin de siècle, allegory

items.title: The Poor Fisherman
items.description_narrative: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes's iconic painting depicts a lone figure in a desolate landscape, embodying themes of melancholic contemplation and humanity's quiet struggle. Its monumental simplicity and dreamlike atmosphere established a powerful new direction in painting, influencing later Symbolist artists.
items.tags: symbolism, melancholic, contemplation, solitude, landscape, early modern, French art

items.title: Flaming June
items.description_narrative: Frederic Leighton's iconic work depicts a woman in a vibrant orange gown, asleep in a dream-like, contorted pose. Bathed in the golden light of a setting sun, the figure is positioned against a distant, serene Mediterranean seascape.
items.tags: sleeping woman, aestheticism, victorian art, classical, mediterranean, orange, opulence, repose

items.title: The Roses of Heliogabalus
items.description_narrative: Lawrence Alma-Tadema's "The Roses of Heliogabalus" captures a decadent scene from ancient Rome. It depicts guests at an imperial banquet being overwhelmed by a deluge of rose petals, a moment of luxurious excess attributed to Emperor Elagabalus.
items.tags: ancient Rome, historical painting, academic art, decadence, opulence, drama, Victorian art

items.title: Circe Invidiosa
items.description_narrative: The sorceress Circe pours emerald poison into the sea to transform her rival Scylla into a monster, her jealous rage rendered in swirling green drapery and glowing pigment. Waterhouse drew on Ovid's Metamorphoses to cast Circe as one of literature's archetypal femme fatales.
items.tags: waterhouse, circe, greek mythology, sorceress, symbolism, femme fatale

items.title: Hope
items.description_narrative: A blindfolded woman perches atop a globe, bent over a lyre with all its strings broken but one, straining to hear a faint note of music amid apparent desolation. Watts intended the figure not as despair but as hope persisting against the odds, and the image became one of the most widely reproduced allegorical paintings of the Victorian era.
items.tags: watts, allegory, hope, blindfold, lyre, symbolism, victorian

items.title: The Caress (Les Caresses)
items.description_narrative: A leopard-bodied sphinx with a woman's head presses affectionately against an androgynous youth clutching a staff, an enigmatic scene drawn from the myth of Oedipus. Khnopff's fusion of sensuality and menace made it one of the signature images of Belgian Symbolism.
items.tags: khnopff, sphinx, oedipus, symbolism, belgian, myth, sensuality

items.title: The Wheel of Fortune
items.description_narrative: Burne-Jones depicted the goddess Fortuna turning a great wheel bearing a king, a slave, and a poet, illustrating the medieval idea that all worldly rank is subject to chance. Commissioned by his patron Arthur Balfour, the painting is now held by the Musée d'Orsay.

items.title: Echo and Narcissus
items.description_narrative: Waterhouse illustrated the Ovidian myth of the youth Narcissus, transfixed by his own reflection in a pool, while the nymph Echo looks on in unrequited longing. The painting is held by the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool.

items.title: Madonna
items.description_narrative: Munch portrayed a nude woman in a trance-like pose ringed by a halo-like red arc, conflating religious icon with erotic vision as part of his cycle 'The Frieze of Life.' He painted several versions of the composition; this one is held by the National Museum of Norway in Oslo.
